tagline: We make a number for every game. We bet the ones where the market's wrong.

games.take: The Thursday night rematch, a month after these two tied 27-27 in October — the winner takes the NFC East lead and the head-to-head tiebreaker. The Giants are 5-2-1 and 6-2 against the spread behind a defense that just made Arvell Reese NFC Defensive Player of the Week; Washington is 2-5-1 and still looking for its first road win. Both quarterbacks are cleared: J.J. McCarthy practiced fully after the hip pointer that pulled him out for a series in Philadelphia, and Jayden Daniels practiced fully with his left elbow listed. The injuries bite Washington harder — Terry McLaurin is out for the season, center Lucas Patrick is out (concussion), and the ground game is down two backs. Then the weather: rain through the game window at MetLife, 52°F at kickoff, northeast wind 12 mph gusting to 29 mph — the total has already fallen from 43 to 41.5, so the market has priced the rain in. No price on the side clears our 0.75% bar; the least-bad number in the game is Washington +114 on the moneyline (-2.1% EV). No true edge, but the lean is Washington +2.5: the points plus a wet, low-total game keep it close.
games.title: Commanders at Giants: the rainy TNF rematch
games.verdict: LEAN: WAS +2.5 — no true edge, but the least-bad price in the game and the weather keeps it low-scoring.
games.weather: Rain through the game window, 52°F at kickoff, NE wind 12 mph gusting to 29 mph. No NWS watch or warning.

games.take: Detroit (7-3) visits a Washington team (4-8) that has lost five straight and is on the second night of a back-to-back after a loss at Indiana. The Pistons are without Jalen Duren (hamstring), though he has played only two games this season. Washington's bright spot is Kyshawn George, who has scored 20 or more in three straight, and Anthony Davis has played both games since his ankle sprain. The number says what it is: Detroit is an 80.1% favorite on the devigged Pinnacle fair, and the best US price on the Pistons (-430) still sits at -1.3% EV — no true edge, and laying -10.5 on the road with a big number pays nothing to get wrong. The lean is Detroit: the far better team, and the least-bad price in the game.
games.title: Pistons at Wizards: the big road favorite
games.verdict: LEAN: DET — no true edge, but the Pistons are the far better team and -430 is the least-bad price in the game.

games.take: Philadelphia (9-3) hosts a tired Toronto team (5-6) on the second night of a back-to-back after blowing a 22-point home lead against Boston on Wednesday — and the Raptors are without Scottie Barnes and Kawhi Leonard. The question is on the favorite's side: Joel Embiid (foot) and LeBron James (back) are both listed questionable, and the Sixers have no healthy backup center. The spread has already moved with that uncertainty (from -10.5 this morning to -8.5). The devigged Pinnacle fair has Philadelphia at 76.1%, and the best US price (-331) is -0.9% EV — no true edge. The lean is Philadelphia: the healthier, deeper team at home against a short-handed opponent on a back-to-back.
games.title: Raptors at 76ers: tired Toronto, banged-up Philly
games.verdict: LEAN: PHI — no true edge, but the 76ers are the deeper team at home against a short-handed back-to-back opponent.

games.take: The night's best NBA game, on NBA TV: Minnesota (8-3) hosts Dallas (7-4) with Cooper Flagg taking on one of the league's better defenses. The Timberwolves are doing it without Anthony Edwards, out after knee surgery, and have lost only three games anyway. The devigged Pinnacle fair has Minnesota at 67.8%, and the best US price (-214) is -0.6% EV — the closest any NBA price came to the bar tonight, and still under it. The total (226.5) is the highest on the slate. No true edge, but the lean is Minnesota: home court, the better defense, and the least-bad price in the game.
games.title: Mavericks at Timberwolves: Flagg vs the Wolves' defense
games.verdict: LEAN: MIN — no true edge, but the Timberwolves are the better defensive team at home and -214 is the least-bad price in the game.

games.take: Phoenix (4-6) hosts Charlotte (4-7) in the late game, and the Hornets are the most short-handed team on the slate: Brandon Miller (groin/hip), Dennis Schroder, and Kon Knueppel are all out, and Charlotte has lost three straight road games. Grayson Allen returns for the Suns. The devigged Pinnacle fair has Phoenix at 67.5%, but the best US price on the Suns (-245) is -5.0% EV — the worst favorite price on the board. The least-bad price in the game is actually on the other side: Charlotte +205 on the moneyline (-0.9% EV). No true edge, but the lean is Charlotte +6.5: the points plus a short-handed-but-live dog against a favorite the market has overpriced.
games.title: Hornets at Suns: the short-handed dog
games.verdict: LEAN: CHA +6.5 — no true edge, but Charlotte's +205 moneyline is the least-bad price in the game.

games.take: The Thursday night American Conference game in Tampa, and the line has already told a story: Memphis opened -7.5 and has been bet down to -3.5, through the key number of 4, while the total climbed from 48.5 to 50.5. Memphis (7-2) comes off a bye, has won the last five meetings, gains 514 yards a game, and quarterback Marcus Stokes has 25 touchdown passes. South Florida (6-3) lost to East Carolina last week, averages 316 yards a game — but its defense allows just 313 yards a game and has thrown only two interceptions all season. The steam toward the Bulls is a signal to investigate, not an edge: our devigged Pinnacle fair still has Memphis at 62.2%, and the best US price on the Tigers (-168) is -0.7% EV — no true edge. The lean is Memphis -3.5: the better offense, off a bye, with the line now sitting under a field goal.
games.title: Memphis at South Florida: the line that moved four points
games.verdict: LEAN: MEM -3.5 — no true edge, but the Tigers are the better offense off a bye and the line has dropped under a field goal.
games.weather: Cloudy and dry, 73°F at kickoff, light west wind. No NWS watch or warning.

games.matchup: Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns @ UL Monroe Warhawks
games.our_fair: Ragin' Cajuns 77.9% / Warhawks 22.1% (devigged Pinnacle fair, moneyline)
games.take: The Battle on the Bayou for the Wooden Boot, and Louisiana has taken it home in seven of the last eight meetings — Monroe's lone win came in 2022. Louisiana is the 77.9% favorite on the devigged Pinnacle fair, and its moneyline is the closest thing to an edge on the entire slate: -345 at one US book is +0.4% EV, still under our 0.75% bar. The spread (-10) and total (48.5) are both fairly priced. No true edge, but the lean is Louisiana: the better team, the series history, and the only price tonight that even sniffed fair value.
games.title: Louisiana at UL Monroe: the Wooden Boot
games.verdict: LEAN: LOU — no true edge, but the Ragin' Cajuns are the better team and -345 is the closest price to fair value on the slate.
games.weather: Sunny and dry, ~74°F at kickoff, NW wind 5-15 mph. No NWS watch or warning (a fire danger statement ends at 6 p.m., before kickoff).
